S1.name: Shipment 1
S1.lede: The dedicated-box letter: one R640, one Ubuntu guest, no RayNu-V engineer in the room.

Final.name: Final SKU
Final.lede: Everything a professional operator expects from a PowerEdge hypervisor, through cluster and VMware migration. If it is not a row here, it is not the product.

waves.why: What Everest and M8.0–M8.8 left on the R640. Regression set for every later wave.
Never open new work with an iron loop half-done. The port 4 cable arrives, this closes.
Cheap, in code just touched; each would have saved a day in October.
M8.5 in ADR-018 terms. Everything after depends on it.
The first "walk away from the rack" moment. Needs wave 3.

waves.theme: A customer can be let in
waves.why: Security and audit together; what diligence asks for first. Host-heavy, overlaps wave 4 iron time.
Needs C8 so an update keeps guests. Signing (A5) needs a key decision from the operator.
Performance and capacity. B8 before B7: SMP on an 8259 is misery.
Tier 1 only. Host work plus one iron screenshot.
72 hours on the R640 with a guest under load, then rerun wave 0. The S1 release.

waves.theme: Port roles and the one-cable customer
waves.why: First Final wave; the question the lab asked on 2026-10-19.
Windows is the iron thread; the rest is host-first.
NVMe first; it is TCG-proven already.
TPM measured boot is the only iron row.
VLAN first; it unlocks most customer topologies.
Watchdog is the iron row; Tier 2 Redfish stays non-blocking (ADR-005).
Live migration is the iron thread; hot-add rides with it.
[V] north star. Runs beside every wave; never waits for one.
